summary.text: Yusef Salaam represents a Council district in Manhattan that includes Morningside Heights, West Harlem, Hamilton Heights, Harlem and East Harlem.
His Council biography describes him as a poet, activist and speaker who was one of the five young men tried and convicted in the 1989 "Central Park jogger" case.

paragraphs.text: Salaam was fifteen when he was tried and convicted in 1989, and his Council biography says the five spent between seven and 13 years in prison for crimes they did not commit, until their sentences were overturned in 2002.
It says they later received a settlement from New York City and have been profiled in the Ken Burns documentary The Central Park Five and the Netflix series When They See Us.
The biography says he has advocated for criminal justice reform, prison reform and the abolition of juvenile solitary confinement and capital punishment.
He was awarded an honorary doctorate in 2014, received a Lifetime Achievement Award from President Barack Obama in 2016, and wrote the memoir Better, Not Bitter and co-authored Punching the Air.
